messages:
natalie_support: Customer hitting intermittent 502 bursts from hybrid app (iOS app with embedded WKWebView + our web SDK). They report timestamps and a few user IDs but no reqids. Can we list exactly what to ask for?
paul_mobile: ugh. Hybrid webview usually strips headers. do we know if it's a proxy or CDN in front? any sample request time windows?
natalie_support: customer says spikes around 12:00-12:20 UTC, ~10 failures in 2 mins. app uses an in-house proxy then CloudFront. no raw HAR attached. asking for explicit steps we can hand to non-dev user.
anil_sre: short checklist we can send them: 1) capture a HAR from the webview (or network trace) 2) grab the SDK console session id / debug token 3) provide one failing + one succeeding request timestamp and the device time zone. Also ask for exact app version and proxy host.
kevin_eng: to be concrete: ask them to find the request id in these places (in order):
- Embedded webview: open remote inspector -> network -> click the failed request -> look in "Response Headers" for x-redwood-reqid or x-request-id. Screenshot.
- iOS native fallback: collect sysdiagnose + Console.app logs around the timestamps (sysdiagnose includes network logs).
- Android: logcat grep for "RESPONSE_ID" or our SDK tag and include lines + timestamps.
paul_mobile: for non-devs, give one-click instructions for HAR from WKWebView: enable Safari > Develop > connect device > open Web Inspector > Network tab > reproduce > Export as HAR. Add short gif would help.
natalie_support: good. also need a curl repro: simplest minimal curl that simulates the failing header set and body. ask them to run locally if they can. example snippet to give them below.
anil_sre: paste curl and mention redaction: never include Authorization tokens in public thread. replace with <<REDACTED_TOKEN>>. then ask to attach the raw output including headers (-i) so we can see response codes and any response headers.
deply-bot: debug-token created for session natalie-support-1767005678 at 2026-03-18T15:34:10Z :token:DXb-EXAMPLE
kevin_eng: sample curl to share with customer (tell them to run from a terminal and paste output):
```
curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <<REDACTED_TOKEN>>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.45" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Debug-Token: DXb-EXAMPLE" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
kevin_eng: key headers to look for in response: x-redwood-reqid, x-redwood-cache, server, via. If 502 returned, copy the response body and any HTML error page too.
paul_mobile: mention how to get a debug token from our SDK UI: Console -> Sessions -> click session -> "Create debug token". For mobile SDKs they can call SDK.debug.generateDebugToken() if they have a dev build. Include that as optional.
anil_sre: if proxy strips IDs, ask customer to set a temporary passthrough: add header X-Forwarded-Request-Id: 12345-please and run one call. If that shows up in our logs we correlate quickly. If they can't change proxy, a pcap from their edge (tcpdump/charles) + timestamps works.
natalie_support: I'll send customer a compact template to paste in their reply: 1) screenshot of Network row showing request and response headers, 2) HAR or pcap file, 3) one failing curl output (-i) that uses DXb-EXAMPLE debug token, 4) device model + OS + app version + proxy host, 5) exact failure timestamps in ISO with timezone.
kevin_eng: also request one successful example close in time to compare headers (helps rule out transient downstream 502 from CDN).
natalie_support: perfect. I'll ping customer now and request those 5 items, and remind them to redact auth tokens before posting. Will escalate to you all once they attach. :thumbsup:
kevin_eng: thanks — if they send anything noisy I can run a quick grep across logs for the timestamps + X-Redwood-Debug-Token.
anil_sre: FYI if we get the debug token + reqid we can pull full trace with `redwood trace get <reqid> --debug-token DXb-EXAMPLE` and attach console-level trace to the case.
natalie_support: copied. closing this thread for now, will reopen with attachments when customer replies.
